questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A government school is built by private builders in a residential neighbourhood. The builders ignore the effects of noise and disturbance. Why does a free market fail to take into account these external costs of building the school?

options.A: Education is a public good which benefits society.
options.B: Few people who live near the school object to the building.
options.C: The government believes schools should be built privately.
options.D: These costs are not paid for by the builders.

questions.questionText: In all market structures, what must firms equate to ensure allocative efficiency?

options.A: average cost and average revenue
options.B: average cost and marginal revenue
options.C: marginal cost and average revenue
options.D: marginal cost and marginal revenue

questions.questionText: In the diagram a consumer’s budget line shifts from JK to GH. J quantity of G good Y O K H quantity of good X Which statement must be correct?

options.A: There has been an increase in the consumer’s money income.
options.B: There has been a decrease in the consumer’s real income.
options.C: Good Y has become relatively more expensive.
options.D: The price of good X has increased.

questions.questionText: The table shows substitution and income effects for a normal good and for an inferior good as the price of the good changes. Which combination is correct? demand change from demand change from type of good price change substitution effect income effect

options.A: inferior fall negative positive
options.B: inferior rise negative negative
options.C: normal fall positive positive
options.D: normal rise positive negative

questions.questionText: A government imposes a $10 tax on each unit produced of a product. How will this affect the firm?

options.A: Its average cost will rise by less than $10.
options.B: Its marginal cost will remain unchanged.
options.C: Its minimum average cost output will be lower.
options.D: Its minimum average cost output will be unchanged.

questions.questionText: According to oligopoly theory, what is not likely to characterise the behaviour of firms in the industry?

options.A: matching any price cuts made by their rivals
options.B: matching any price rises made by their rivals
options.C: selling a range of similar but differentiated products
options.D: the ability to earn supernormal profit

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a monopolist whose only cost of production is a fixed cost. What will be the monopolist’s profit maximising price? costs / revenue D C B A ATC O MR AR output
Company R manufactures steel. Company S produces ships. Company T operates oil tankers. Company V operates cruise liners. Which statement is correct?

options.A: If R takes over S, this is an example of forwards vertical integration.
options.B: If S takes over V, this is an example of backwards vertical integration.
options.C: If T takes over S, this is an example of diversification.
options.D: If V takes over S, this is an example of horizontal integration.

questions.questionText: A monopolist chooses an output that maximises profits and makes normal profits. What must be correct at the output chosen?

options.A: Average cost equals average revenue.
options.B: Average revenue equals marginal revenue.
options.C: Marginal cost is at a minimum.
options.D: The monopolist is allocatively efficient.

questions.questionText: A firm operates in an imperfectly competitive market. The prices of its products are determined by the maximum price each consumer is willing to pay. What describes this pricing method?

options.A: kinked demand curve
options.B: limit pricing
options.C: price discrimination
options.D: price leadership

questions.questionText: What is an argument for government policy which allows companies to take over other companies?

options.A: It allows firms to borrow from the banking system.
options.B: It encourages companies to act to promote productive efficiency.
options.C: It ensures wage rates will rise.
options.D: It provides income and employment for investment bankers.

questions.questionText: A government imposes a maximum price for electricity. Which statement justifying this measure might be considered valid on economic grounds?

options.A: It will encourage electricity suppliers to invest in additional capacity.
options.B: It will increase the incentive for consumers to conserve energy.
options.C: It will prevent the monopolistic exploitation of consumers.
options.D: It will prevent the rationing of electricity through power cuts.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the change in a market when a government places a production quota OQ t on the quantity of a good that has previously traded at quantity OQ. price S V W X Z Y D O Q Q t quantity Which welfare loss results from the government’s policy?

options.A: W + V B W + X C X + Z D Y + Z

questions.questionText: Which policy by a government would increase the negative externalities that result from cigarette smoking?

options.A: a ban on cigarette advertising
options.B: a ban on cigarette smoking in public places
options.C: a ban on substitutes for cigarettes
options.D: a ban on the sale of cigarettes

questions.questionText: A teacher currently earns $30000 but would be willing to continue to do the job provided she earned at least $25000. She prefers to stay in her teaching job than change to her next best alternative employment as an accountant where she could earn $40000. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Her economic rent as a teacher is $5000.
options.B: Her economic rent as an accountant is $10000.
options.C: Her transfer earnings as a teacher are $30000.
options.D: Her transfer earnings as an accountant are $15000.

questions.questionText: What will increase the power of a trade union, allowing it to increase wages without reducing the employment of its members in a particular industry?

options.A: The economy is experiencing a fall in the price of capital.
options.B: The economy is experiencing rising employment.
options.C: The price elasticity of demand for the industry’s goods is equal to 1.
options.D: The price elasticity of demand for the industry’s goods is greater than 1.

questions.questionText: The table shows the number of workers employed by four firms in the same industry, the average number of hours worked each day and the total output each firm produces each day. Which firm’s workers have the highest productivity? average number number of total output per of hours worked workers day (units) per day
Which stage of the business (trade) cycle is most likely to be characterised by an increasing negative output gap?

options.A: boom
options.B: recession
options.C: recovery
options.D: trough

questions.questionText: Which characteristics are typical features of the least developed countries? dominant sector export terms of trade of industry earnings over time

options.A: primary stable stable
options.B: primary unstable unstable
options.C: secondary stable rising
options.D: secondary unstable falling

questions.questionText: What is central to economic growth but not necessarily to economic development?

options.A: an expansion of the range of economic choices available to individuals
options.B: an increase in Gross Domestic Product
options.C: the eradication of absolute poverty
options.D: the satisfaction of basic needs amongst the whole population

questions.questionText: What would be the essential element in listing countries in order of their standards of living during a particular year?

options.A: a deduction for profits transmitted abroad from the figures for Gross National Product
options.B: allowance for different rates of population growth
options.C: an adjustment for the inflation rates of different countries
options.D: the use of purchasing power parity exchange rates

questions.questionText: A government wished to increase demand in an economy in an attempt to reduce unemployment. Which policy is most likely to achieve this?

options.A: establishing greater health and safety rules for manufacturers
options.B: increasing income tax
options.C: increasing the rate of interest
options.D: subsidising the building of new houses

questions.questionText: What would be an increase in leakages or withdrawals from the circular flow of income?

options.A: increase in government spending on anti-smoking campaigns
options.B: increase in spending on imports of luxury cars
options.C: increase in spending on transfer payments
options.D: increase in wages paid to government employees

questions.questionText: What is used to measure the deflationary gap?

options.A: the increase in injections needed to reach full employment
options.B: the public sector borrowing requirement
options.C: the rate of deflation
options.D: the rate of unemployment

questions.questionText: The following data describes an economy’s consumption function. income consumption ($m) ($m) 100 90 140 122 180 154 220 186 What can be deduced about the value of the marginal propensity to consume in this economy?

options.A: It increases as income increases.
options.B: It decreases as income increases.
options.C: It is 0.90.
options.D: It is 0.80.

questions.questionText: In which circumstance will there be an immediate increase in the domestic money supply?

options.A: A consumer takes advantage of an overdraft facility to buy a car.
options.B: A consumer uses a reserve of cash to buy a car.
options.C: A consumer uses a reserve of Euros to buy a car abroad.
options.D: A consumer uses their current bank account balance to buy a car.

questions.questionText: The turning point on the Kuznets Curve for income inequality has been estimated to be in the region of US $10500. For a country that has a GDP per capita of $8000, which is most likely?

options.A: A reduction in GDP per capita will have no effect on income inequality.
options.B: A reduction in GDP per capita will increase income inequality.
options.C: An increase in GDP per capita will have no effect on income inequality.
options.D: An increase in GDP per capita will increase income inequality.

questions.questionText: Which macroeconomic policy aims are most likely to complement one another?

options.A: high growth and low inflation
options.B: high growth and low unemployment
options.C: low inflation and low unemployment
options.D: low unemployment and a balance of trade surplus

questions.questionText: All else remaining unchanged, what would result in an outflow of capital funds from a country?

options.A: a fall in the country’s rate of inflation
options.B: an expected appreciation of the country’s exchange rate
options.C: an increase in foreign interest rates
